dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: The complete proposition: there exists a real constant C at least 1, chosen before all probability spaces and families, such that every finite nonempty independent centered unit-variance family satisfying the stated sub-Gaussian condition obeys the displayed two-sided Lp estimate for every coefficient vector and every real p at least 2.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies all quantifiers, hypotheses, and both inequality directions of the target.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef004

binders: There exists a real constant C, chosen outside and before every subsequent universal quantifier.
For every index type I and sample type Omega, where I is finite and nonempty and Omega carries a measurable-space structure.
For every probability measure mu on Omega and every real-valued family X = (X_i) indexed by I.
For every real coefficient family a = (a_i) indexed by I and every real p.
hypotheses: For every i, X_i is measurable and admits a real K_i > 0 such that exp(X_i^2/K_i^2) is integrable and has mu-integral at most 2.
For every i, X_i is integrable and centered: integral X_i dmu = 0.
The indexed functions X_i are jointly independent with respect to mu.
conclusions: The Euclidean coefficient norm is a lower bound: sqrt(sum_i a_i^2) <= ||sum_i a_i X_i||_{L^p(mu)}.
The same Lp norm has the upper bound ||sum_i a_i X_i||_{L^p(mu)} <= C * (max_i ||X_i||_{psi_2}) * sqrt(p) * sqrt(sum_i a_i^2).
mathematical_definitions: The random linear combination is S(omega) = sum over all i in I of a_i X_i(omega).
The coefficient scale is ||a||_2 = sqrt(sum over all i in I of a_i^2).
An ENNReal number t is psi-two admissible for X when X is measurable, t is neither 0 nor infinity, exp(X^2/(t.toReal)^2) is integrable, and its mu-integral is at most 2.
The individual psi-two gauge ||X||_{psi_2} is the ENNReal infimum of all admissible t.
The family scale max_i ||X_i||_{psi_2} used in the conclusion is concretely the maximum over the nonempty finite index set of the real conversions of those ENNReal gauges.
The displayed Lp quantity is the real-valued lpNorm at exponent ENNReal.ofReal(p); because p >= 2, this is the intended nonnegative exponent p.
translation.proposition_plain_english: There is one universal real constant C >= 1 such that, for every finite nonempty family of jointly independent, integrable, centered, real-valued sub-Gaussian random variables on an arbitrary probability space, each having variance exactly 1, every real coefficient vector a and every real p >= 2 satisfy the two-sided estimate sqrt(sum_i a_i^2) <= ||sum_i a_i X_i||_{L^p(mu)} <= C (max_i ||X_i||_{psi_2}) sqrt(p) sqrt(sum_i a_i^2), where the maximum and sums range over the entire finite index set and the psi-two scale is the infimum of the admissible square-exponential scales defined above.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The index family is required to be finite and nonempty; the proposition does not cover the empty family or infinite families.
The exponent p is a real number restricted to p >= 2; no assertion is made for smaller or negative p.

Every variable must separately be integrable, centered, sub-Gaussian in the stated square-exponential sense, and have variance exactly 1; the implication is vacuous for any family failing one of these premises.
The variables are required to be jointly independent but not identically distributed.
The constant C is existentially quantified before the probability space, family, coefficients, and p, so it is uniform over all of them; it is additionally constrained by C >= 1.
The psi-two family scale is the maximum of ENNReal gauges after conversion to Real, and each gauge is defined by an ENNReal infimum over nonzero finite admissible scales.
The library lpNorm returns 0 for a function that is not almost-everywhere strongly measurable, although the finite sum here is expected to be measurable from the stated measurability of every X_i.
Variance is the real conversion of an extended variance and is imposed to equal exactly 1.
